claim: 29 cHCV and 37 Sustained Virologic Responders (SVR) patients were included in the study.
source: 29 cHCV and 37 Sustained Virologic Responders (SVR, i.e. patients achieving clearance of the virus after therapy) patients were included in the study (Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of patients in each group included in the study.

claim: 62% of the chronic HCV patients received at least one anti-HCV treatment.
source: 62% of the chronic and 100% of the SVR patients received at least one anti-HCV treatment (of those treated, 69% received conventional IFN-ribavirin bitherapy, 31% IFN + direct antiviral agent (DAA), and IFN-free DAA combination therapy alone in the case of a single SVR patient).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentages of treatment received by patient groups.

claim: 100% of the SVR patients received at least one anti-HCV treatment.
source: 62% of the chronic and 100% of the SVR patients received at least one anti-HCV treatment (of those treated, 69% received conventional IFN-ribavirin bitherapy, 31% IFN + direct antiviral agent (DAA), and IFN-free DAA combination therapy alone in the case of a single SVR patient).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that all SVR patients received treatment.

claim: Total lymphocyte numbers were within the normal range for all tested patients (median 2.2 +/- 0.6 G/l).
source: Total lymphocyte numbers were within the normal range for all tested patients (median 2.2 +/- 0.6 G/l).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measurements of lymphocyte counts.

claim: Absolute numbers of CD3+ T cells were significantly increased in cHCV patients (KW p<0.0001).
source: However, absolute numbers of CD3+ were significantly increased in our cohort of cHCV (KW p<0.0001), translating into increased absolute numbers of CD8+ T cells in cHCV patients (KW p=0.0002) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis (p-value) and references a figure showing the data.

claim: Absolute numbers of CD8+ T cells were significantly increased in cHCV patients (KW p=0.0002).
source: However, absolute numbers of CD3+ were significantly increased in our cohort of cHCV (KW p<0.0001), translating into increased absolute numbers of CD8+ T cells in cHCV patients (KW p=0.0002) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis (p-value) and references a figure showing the data.

claim: Co-expression of high levels of CD45RA and CD27 are sufficient to classify naïve T cells in both HD and cHCV patients.
source: Based on prior studies (Alanio et al., 2010; De Rosa et al., 2001) and our confirmatory experiments using 5 phenotypic markers for naïve or memory T cells, we determined that co-expression of high levels of CD45RA and CD27 were sufficient to classify naïve T cells in both HD and cHCV patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies and references confirmatory experiments shown in a figure.

claim: Decreased percentages of naïve CD8+ T cells have previously been reported in cHCV.
source: Decreased percentages of naïve CD8+T cells have previously been reported in cHCV (Shen et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: Decreased percentages of naïve CD8+ T cells were confirmed in age- and CMV-matched chronically infected patients (KW p=0.0007).
source: Here, we confirmed these findings in age- and CMV- matched chronically infected patients (KW p=0.0007, Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: The absolute numbers of naïve CD8+ T cells were within the normal range in cHCV patients after correcting for higher CD8+ T cell numbers.
source: Interestingly, we found that after correcting for the higher CD8+ T cell numbers in cHCV patients, the absolute numbers of naïve CD8+ T cells were within the normal range as determined by the study of healthy donors (Figure 1C).
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis of absolute cell counts shown in a figure.

claim: The lower proportion of naïve T cells in cHCV patients is a result of an expansion of the memory cell compartment.
source: We therefore interpreted the lower proportion of naïve T cells to simply be a result of an expansion of the memory cell compartment.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: There was a significant decrease in sjTREC content of CD8+ T cells in cHCV patients (MW p=0.01).
source: Confirming previous studies, we found a significant decrease in sjTREC content of CD8+ T cells (MW p=0.01, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a figure showing the data.

claim: Naïve CD8+ T cells in cHCV patients showed significantly lower sjTREC content compared to HD (MW p=0.03).
source: Surprisingly, we also observed within the naïve compartment a significantly lower sjTREC content in cHCV patients as compared to HD (MW p=0.03, Figure 1D).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a figure showing the data.

claim: cHCV patients showed a biased Vβ repertoire with increased representation of selected Vβ families.
source: To further characterize this phenotype, we assessed the Vβ distribution within the naïve repertoire of cHCV patients. cHCV patients showed a biased repertoire with increased representation of selected Vβ families.
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis of Vβ distribution in patient samples.

claim: Gini coefficients were increased in cHCV patients (M-W p=0.03).
source: In line with our observation, we found Gini coefficients increased in cHCV patients (M-W p=0.03, see Material and Methods for details of calculation) (Figure 1G).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a figure showing the data.

claim: The data support an overall perturbed naïve CD8+ T cell repertoire in cHCV patients, with increased peripheral expansion of selected populations.
source: These data support an overall perturbed naïve CD8+ T cell repertoire in cHCV patients, with increased peripheral expansion of selected populations.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary interpretation of the data presented.

claim: Similar absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells were observed in HD, SVR, and cHCV study groups.
source: While similar absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells were observed in our respective study groups (Figure 2A,B), SVR and cHCV patients showed a more differentiated phenotype (Figure 2C), defined by fewer CD45RA+/CD27+ and increased proportions of memory-phenotype (MP) cells (KW p<0.0001, Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis shown in figures.

claim: SVR and cHCV patients showed a more differentiated phenotype of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: While similar absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells were observed in our respective study groups (Figure 2A,B), SVR and cHCV patients showed a more differentiated phenotype (Figure 2C), defined by fewer CD45RA+/CD27+ and increased proportions of memory-phenotype (MP) cells (KW p<0.0001, Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis shown in figures.

claim: SVR and cHCV patients showed increased proportions of memory-phenotype (MP) Mart1-specific cells (KW p<0.0001).
source: While similar absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells were observed in our respective study groups (Figure 2A,B), SVR and cHCV patients showed a more differentiated phenotype (Figure 2C), defined by fewer CD45RA+/CD27+ and increased proportions of memory-phenotype (MP) cells (KW p<0.0001, Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: MP cells in cHCV patients were mostly of central-memory (CD45RA-CD27+) phenotype.
source: Of note, these MP cells were mostly of central-memory (CD45RA-CD27+) phenotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Precursor frequencies of naïve-phenotype Mart1-specific cells were comparable across different study groups.
source: Also, when considering only naïve-phenotype Mart1-specific cells, precursor frequencies were still comparable across the different study groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Immunoscope analysis of Mart1-specific T cells from one HCV patient showed a restricted repertoire of naïve T cells with evidence of an expanded Vβ clonotype in memory cells.
source: We were able to purify sufficient numbers of Mart1-specific naïve- and memory- phenotype CD8+ T cells from one HCV patient to perform an immunoscope analysis on the Vβ chain usage (Figure 2E). In line with our data in bulk T cells populations (Figure 1), we observed a restricted repertoire of Mart1-specific naïve T cells, with evidence of an expanded Vβ clonotype in memory cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The data argue in favor of MP cells being the progeny of a perturbed naïve T cell repertoire.
source: These data argue in favor of MP cells being the progeny of a perturbed naïve T cell repertoire.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: High proportions of T cells with a memory-phenotype were found in both self (Mart1- and hTERT-specific) and viral (CMV-, Ebola- and HIV-specific) antigen-inexperienced populations of cHCV patients as compared to healthy donors.
source: Here again, we found high proportions of T cells with a memory-phenotype in both self (Mart1- and hTERT- specific) and viral (CMV-, Ebola- and HIV- specific) antigen-inexperienced populations of cHCV patients as compared to healthy donors (representative plots are shown in Figure 3A and B; and combined results from 2–6 individuals per group in Figure 3C; self-specific: KW p<0.001; non-self-specific: KW p=0.009).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: MP cells found in cHCV patients were preferentially of CD45RA-CD27+ central memory phenotype.
source: When subsetted using CD45RA and CD27 phenotypic markers, the MP cells found in cHCV patients were preferentially of CD45RA-CD27+ central memory phenotype (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Sequential samples from five patients who achieved cure suggested that immune restoration of the naïve compartment is possible (positive time dependency p-value p=0.03).
source: Sequential samples (available from five patients who achieved cure) suggested that immune restoration of the naïve compartment is possible (positive time dependency p-value p=0.03, Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing longitudinal data.

claim: There was a statistically significant recovery of naïve antigen-specific CD8+ T cells as a function of time in the cross-sectional cohort (MW p=0.04).
source: Testing our observation in our cross-sectional cohort, we replicated our findings, showing a statistically significant recovery of naïve antigen-specific CD8+ T cells as a function of time (MW p=0.04; Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a figure showing the data.

claim: The differentiated cells within the perturbed repertoire of cHCV patients are a reflection of active HCV infection, and likely not a result of cross-reactivity or true memory T cell differentiation.
source: These results indicate that the differentiated cells within the perturbed repertoire of cHCV patients are a reflection of active HCV infection, and likely not a result of cross-reactivity or true memory T cell differentiation.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: Phenotypic changes (low CD5 expression) were significant for the comparison between CD45RA+/CD27+ naïve CD8+ T cells in cHCV vs HD (KW p=0.02).
source: We observed phenotypic changes (i.e. low CD5 expression) that were significant for the comparison between CD45RA+/CD27+ naïve CD8+ T cells in cHCV vs HD (KW p=0.02, Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: TCR stimulation induced a strong p-ERK signal in naïve cells from seven of sixteen cHCV patients tested (MW p=0.03).
source: While only weak induction of phosphorylated ERK (p-ERK) could be observed in HD during the first hour of stimulation, TCR stimulation induced a strong p-ERK signal in naïve cells from seven of sixteen cHCV patients tested (histograms from one responding cHCV and one HD are shown in Figure 5C; MW p=0.03, Figure 5D).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: Higher percentages of cells expressing CD25 were observed on naïve CD8+ T cells from cHCV as compared to HD after 24 hr stimulation (MW p=0.02).
source: Using the same stimulation protocol, we investigated expression of activation markers (i.e., CD25, CD69) measured after 24 hr stimulation. Consistent with p-ERK data, we observed higher percentages of cells expressing CD25 on naïve CD8+ T cells from cHCV as compared to HD (representative example from one cHCV and one HD are shown in Figure 5E; MW p=0.02, Figure 5F).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: Increased percentages of naïve CD8 T cells undergoing activation-induced cell death were observed in cHCV patients as compared to HD (MW p=0.002).
source: We also observed increased percentages of naïve CD8 T cells undergoing activation-induced cell death – as assessed by active caspase 3 staining after 24 hr - in cHCV patients as compared to HD (MW p=0.002; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a supplementary figure showing the data.

claim: When PBMCs from HD were exposed to blocking anti-CD5 Abs prior to TCR stimulation, increased levels of p-ERK were observed after 5 min (Wilcoxon p=0.007).
source: When PBMCs from HD were exposed to blocking anti-CD5 Abs (αCD5) prior to TCR stimulation, we observed (i) increased levels of p-ERK after 5 min (Wilcoxon p=0.007, Figure 5G), (ii) increased CD25 expression after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.03, Figure 5H), and (iii) increased percentages of dying naïve CD8 T cells as assessed by active caspase 3 staining after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.003) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: When PBMCs from HD were exposed to blocking anti-CD5 Abs prior to TCR stimulation, increased CD25 expression was observed after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.03).
source: When PBMCs from HD were exposed to blocking anti-CD5 Abs (αCD5) prior to TCR stimulation, we observed (i) increased levels of p-ERK after 5 min (Wilcoxon p=0.007, Figure 5G), (ii) increased CD25 expression after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.03, Figure 5H), and (iii) increased percentages of dying naïve CD8 T cells as assessed by active caspase 3 staining after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.003) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: When PBMCs from HD were exposed to blocking anti-CD5 Abs prior to TCR stimulation, increased percentages of dying naïve CD8 T cells were observed after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.003).
source: When PBMCs from HD were exposed to blocking anti-CD5 Abs (αCD5) prior to TCR stimulation, we observed (i) increased levels of p-ERK after 5 min (Wilcoxon p=0.007, Figure 5G), (ii) increased CD25 expression after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.03, Figure 5H), and (iii) increased percentages of dying naïve CD8 T cells as assessed by active caspase 3 staining after 24 hr (Wilcoxon p=0.003) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a supplementary figure showing the data.

claim: When αCD5 was applied to cHCV patients, no further increase in TCR-induced activation was observed.
source: By contrast, when αCD5 was applied to the cHCV patients, we observed no further increase in TCR-induced activation (Figure 5—figure supplement 4 A–D).
evidence: The manuscript describes analysis shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: The data provide direct evidence for a negative role of CD5 on TCR-induced activation and activation-induced cell death.
source: These data provide direct evidence for a negative role of CD5 on TCR-induced activation and activation-induced cell death, and support the concept that CD5 molecule is responsible, in part, for the hyperactivation phenotype observed in naive T cells of cHCV patients.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: Low expression of CD5 on naïve T cells in cHCV patients results in dysregulation of the homeostatic TCR threshold.
source: Together, these data support a model where low expression of CD5 on naïve T cells in cHCV patients results in dysregulation of the homeostatic TCR threshold.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary interpretation of the data presented.

claim: Increased percentages of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells were observed when expanded from PBMCs of cHCV patients as compared to those from HD (cHCV vs. HD, Day 8, M-W p=0.02, cHCV vs HD, Day 11, M-W p=0.009).
source: After 8–11 days of in vitro priming, we observed increased percentages of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells when expanded from PBMCs of cHCV patients as compared to those from HD (cHCV vs. HD, Day 8, M-W p=0.02, cHCV vs HD, Day 11, M-W p=0.009, Figure 6A and B; individual FACS plots for all donors are provided in Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: The positive impact of chronic infection on naïve T cell expansion was titratable, with more striking differences in the proportion of MP cells after expansion observed when cells were primed with high doses of peptide (Day 8, M-W p=0.03).
source: The positive impact of chronic infection on naïve T cell expansion was titratable, with more striking differences in the proportion of MP cells after expansion observed when cells were primed with high doses of peptide (Sprent and Surh, 2011) (Day 8, M-W p=0.03; Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a supplementary figure showing the data.

claim: Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells generated from cHCV patients express slightly higher amounts of granzyme B (MW p=0.02).
source: Finally, we found that the Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells generated from cHCV patients express slightly higher amounts of granzyme B (representative example from three cHCV and three HD is shown in Figure 6C; MW p=0.02, Figure 6D).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: Hyperreactive preimmune repertoire was supported by observation of increased secretion of IFNγ by freshly isolated and antigen-restimulated cells from cHCV donors (2-way Anova p=0.0002).
source: Hyperreactive preimmune repertoire was further supported by our observation of increased secretion of IFNγ by freshly isolated and antigen-restimulated cells – shown for Mart1, hTERT and CMV peptides in tumor-free, CMV-seronegative cHCV donors (2-way Anova p=0.0002; Figure 6E and F).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references figures showing the data.

claim: Low levels of CD5 on naïve-phenotype cells from cHCV donors allow low-affinity interactions with non-cognate antigens to result in T cell differentiation.
source: Together, our results favor a model where low levels of CD5 on naïve-phenotype cells from cHCV donors allow low-affinity interactions with non-cognate antigens to result in T cell differentiation, thereby providing an explanation for the increased frequency of MP cells in cHCV patients.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary interpretation of the data presented.

claim: Qualitative alterations of the CD8+ T cell preimmune repertoire in cHCV patients may result in a boosted response to cognate immune stimulation.
source: Additionally, our data indicate that qualitative alterations of the CD8+ T cell preimmune repertoire in cHCV patients may result in a boosted response to cognate immune stimulation.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: 18 cHBV patients were collected for testing preimmune repertoire perturbations.
source: Testing our ability to identify preimmune repertoire perturbations in other clinical conditions, we collected 18 cHBV patients using standard sampling procedures.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of cHBV patients collected.

claim: cHBV patients showed decreased percentages of bulk naïve CD8+ T cells (MW p=0.009).
source: We found normal percentages of CD3+CD8+ T cells (data not shown), and decreased percentages of bulk naïve CD8+ T cells (MW p=0.009, Figure 5—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a supplementary figure showing the data.

claim: cHBV patients demonstrated lower absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells as compared to HD (MW p=0.003).
source: We demonstrated lower absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells in HBV patients (MW p=0.003, Figure 5—figure supplement 5B) and increased frequencies of MP Mart1-specific cells (MW p=0.03, Figure 5—figure supplement 5C) as compared to HD, but (ii) similar levels of CD5 expression (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5D), and (iii) a similar a activation profile of bulk naïve T cells as compared to HD (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5E).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a supplementary figure showing the data.

claim: cHBV patients showed increased frequencies of MP Mart1-specific cells as compared to HD (MW p=0.03).
source: We demonstrated lower absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells in HBV patients (MW p=0.003, Figure 5—figure supplement 5B) and increased frequencies of MP Mart1-specific cells (MW p=0.03, Figure 5—figure supplement 5C) as compared to HD, but (ii) similar levels of CD5 expression (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5D), and (iii) a similar a activation profile of bulk naïve T cells as compared to HD (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5E).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a supplementary figure showing the data.

claim: cHBV patients showed similar levels of CD5 expression as compared to HD (MW p=ns).
source: We demonstrated lower absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells in HBV patients (MW p=0.003, Figure 5—figure supplement 5B) and increased frequencies of MP Mart1-specific cells (MW p=0.03, Figure 5—figure supplement 5C) as compared to HD, but (ii) similar levels of CD5 expression (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5D), and (iii) a similar a activation profile of bulk naïve T cells as compared to HD (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5E).
evidence: The manuscript provides statistical analysis and references a supplementary figure showing the data.

claim: cHBV patients showed a similar activation profile of bulk naïve T cells as compared to HD (MW p=ns).
source: We demonstrated lower absolute numbers of Mart1-specific CD8+ T cells in HBV patients (MW p=0.003, Figure 5—figure supplement 5B) and increased frequencies of MP Mart1-specific cells (MW p=0.03, Figure 5—figure supplement 5C) as compared to HD, but (ii) similar levels of CD5 expression (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5D), and (iii) a similar a activation profile of bulk naïve T cells as compared to HD (MW p=ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 5E).

claim: Different persistent viral infections of the liver can trigger distinct preimmune repertoire perturbations.
source: These results indicate that different persistent viral infections of the liver can trigger distinct preimmune repertoire perturbations.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: The study provides novel evidence for chronic viral infection as a cause of CD8+ T cell preimmune repertoire dysregulation.
source: Our study provides novel evidence for chronic viral infection as a cause of CD8+ T cell preimmune repertoire dysregulation.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: Naïve CD8+ T cells are dysregulated in the context of cHCV, marked by decreased sjTRECs levels, a restricted Vβ repertoire, and a lower threshold for TCR engagement.
source: Specifically, we demonstrated that naïve CD8+ T cells are dysregulated in the context of cHCV, marked by (i) decreased sjTRECs levels, (ii) a restricted Vβ repertoire, and (iii) a lower threshold for TCR engagement.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: An increased threshold for TCR activation in naïve CD4+ T cells in elderly persons has been proposed as participating in the diminished response to vaccination that occurs with increasing age.
source: An increased threshold for TCR activation in naïve CD4+ T cells in elderly persons has been proposed as participating in the diminished response to vaccination that occurs with increasing age (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: A decreased threshold for TCR activation, secondary to sustained cytokine production, leads to diverse autoimmune manifestations in rheumatoid arthritis patients.
source: Conversely, a decreased threshold for TCR activation, secondary to sustained cytokine production, leads to diverse autoimmune manifestations in rheumatoid arthritis patients (Singh et al., 2009; Deshpande et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Functional defects in the naïve T cell compartment have been documented in HIV-infected individuals, with non-cognate activation of T cells correlating with disease progression.
source: With respect to chronic infection, functional defects in the naïve T cell compartment have also been documented in HIV-infected individuals, with non-cognate activation of T cells correlating with disease progression (Favre et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: cHCV patients are not thought to experience altered thymic output.
source: Of note, cHCV patients are not thought to experience altered thymic output.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge.

claim: The findings provide direct evidence that MP antigen-specific T cells can arise in non-lymphopenic humans.
source: As such, our findings provide direct evidence that MP antigen-specific T cells can arise in non-lymphopenic humans.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: It has been suggested that a high degree of cross-reactivity with environmental antigens is the trigger for differentiation and MP conversion.
source: It has been suggested that a high degree of cross-reactivity with environmental antigens is the trigger for differentiation and MP conversion (Sprent and Surh, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this suggestion.

claim: Cross-reactivity has been reported for human viral peptide / MHC restricted CD4+ T cells in unexposed donors.
source: This finding has been reported for human viral peptide / MHC restricted CD4+ T cells in unexposed donors (Su et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: The antigen-specific inexperienced T cell populations are restored to a naïve phenotype in cured patients.
source: While cross-reactivity is a possible explanation for our findings, we demonstrate in cured patients that the antigen-specific inexperienced T cell populations are restored to a naïve phenotype.
evidence: The manuscript describes findings from the study.

claim: There is evidence for rapid reversibility to a healthy preimmune repertoire after transient lymphopenia.
source: Supporting this conclusion, we note the evidence for rapid reversibility to a healthy preimmune repertoire after transient lymphopenia (Jones et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: Jones et al. studied multiple sclerosis patients and showed an anti-CD52 treatment-induced narrowing of the Vβ repertoire and the dilution of sjTREC after treatment, with a complete restoration of normal levels two years post-therapy.
source: Consistent with our findings, Jones et al. studied multiple sclerosis patients and showed an anti-CD52 (also known by alemtuzumab) treatment-induced narrowing of the Vβ repertoire and the dilution of sjTREC after treatment, with a complete restoration of normal levels two years post-therapy (Jones et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: Infection and inflammation is known to lower the threshold of TCR signaling in memory T cells, making them more sensitive to activation.
source: Infection and inflammation is known to lower the threshold of TCR signaling in memory T cells, making them more sensitive to activation (Richer et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: The effect of infection and inflammation on memory T cells is mediated by inflammatory cytokines.
source: This effect is mediated by inflammatory cytokines (Raué et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: CD5 tunes the TCR signaling threshold in peripheral T cells, with naïve cells expressing higher levels than central memory or effector T cells.
source: CD5 tunes the TCR signaling threshold in peripheral T cells, with naïve cells expressing higher levels than central memory or effector T cells (Tabbekh et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: Hawiger et al demonstrated that anti-CD5 blocking antibodies, or the use of CD5-/- transgenic MOG-specific T cells, resulted in higher sensitivity to experimental autoimmune encephalitis in mice.
source: In mice, Hawiger et al demonstrated that anti-CD5 blocking antibodies, or the use of CD5-/- transgenic MOG-specific T cells, resulted in higher sensitivity to experimental autoimmune encephalitis (Hawiger et al., 2004).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: In B cells, CD5 has been shown to regulate activation and low CD5 expression correlates with high sensitivity to activation induced cell death.
source: In B cells, CD5 has also been shown to regulate activation and low CD5 expression correlates with high sensitivity to activation induced cell death (Tabbekh et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: Elevated levels of inflammatory cytokines may be responsible for the altered CD5 expression on naïve cells in cHCV patients.
source: While not evaluated in our patient cohort, we propose that elevated levels of inflammatory cytokines may be responsible for the altered CD5 expression on naïve cells (Park and Rehermann, 2014).

claim: The combination of low levels of CD5 and increased proportions of MP in inexperienced antigen-specific populations may provide a compounded effect, resulting in a highly reactive CD8+ T cell compartment.
source: The combination of low levels of CD5 and increased proportions of MP in inexperienced antigen-specific populations may provide a compounded effect, resulting in a highly reactive CD8+ T cell compartment.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: Chronic HCV infection facilitates the generation of robust self-specific responses from the pool of preimmune cells.
source: We provide evidence here that chronic HCV infection facilitates the generation of robust self-specific responses from the pool of preimmune cells.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: Circulating self-reactive effector CD8+ T cells may contribute to the systemic immune activation observed during chronic HCV infection.
source: Given the important role for cellular immunity in the pathogenesis of autoimmune manifestations (Palermo et al., 2001), we speculate that circulating self-reactive effector CD8+ T cells may contribute to the systemic immune activation observed during chronic HCV infection, and account for some of the extra-hepatic autoimmune-like manifestations (Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript proposes a hypothesis based on cited literature.

claim: The ability to restore a physiologically normal preimmune repertoire in cured patients may justify early treatment as a means to limit immune-mediated manifestations of the disease.
source: If our prediction is correct, the ability to restore a physiologically normal preimmune repertoire in cured patients may thus justify early treatment as a means to limit immune-mediated manifestations of the disease.
evidence: The manuscript proposes a hypothesis based on the data presented.

claim: Naïve CD8+ T cells are dysregulated during cHCV, with marked perturbations of the preimmune repertoire.
source: In summary, our study demonstrates that naïve CD8+ T cells are dysregulated during cHCV, with marked perturbations of the preimmune repertoire.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: Low levels of CD5 at the surface of naïve T cells and high proportions of memory-phenotype cells represent two mechanisms by which antigen-inexperienced CD8+ T cells are susceptible to stimulation and antigen-induced expansion.
source: Specifically, low levels of CD5 at the surface of naïve T cells, and high proportions of memory-phenotype cells represent two mechanisms by which antigen-inexperienced CD8+ T cells are susceptible to stimulation and antigen-induced expansion.
evidence: The manuscript provides a summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: Chronic infection perturbs immune homeostasis.
source: Chronic infection perturbs immune homeostasis.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a general principle in the abstract.

claim: Prior studies have reported dysregulation of effector and memory cells during chronic infection.
source: While prior studies have reported dysregulation of effector and memory cells, little is known about the effects on naïve T cell populations.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge.

claim: Little is known about the effects of chronic infection on naïve T cell populations.
source: While prior studies have reported dysregulation of effector and memory cells, little is known about the effects on naïve T cell populations.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a gap in knowledge.

claim: cHCV showed normal precursor frequencies of antigen-specific inexperienced CD8+ T cells.
source: cHCV showed normal precursor frequencies, but increased proportions of memory-phenotype inexperienced cells, as compared to healthy donors or cured HCV patients.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: cHCV showed increased proportions of memory-phenotype inexperienced cells, as compared to healthy donors or cured HCV patients.
source: cHCV showed normal precursor frequencies, but increased proportions of memory-phenotype inexperienced cells, as compared to healthy donors or cured HCV patients.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: The observations of increased memory-phenotype inexperienced cells could be explained by low surface expression of CD5, a negative regulator of TCR signaling.
source: These observations could be explained by low surface expression of CD5, a negative regulator of TCR signaling.
evidence: The manuscript states this interpretation in the abstract.

claim: TCR hyperactivation was demonstrated in cHCV patients.
source: Accordingly, we demonstrated TCR hyperactivation and generation of potent CD8+ T cell responses from the altered T cell repertoire of cHCV patients.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: Generation of potent CD8+ T cell responses from the altered T cell repertoire of cHCV patients was demonstrated.
source: Accordingly, we demonstrated TCR hyperactivation and generation of potent CD8+ T cell responses from the altered T cell repertoire of cHCV patients.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: The study provides the first evidence that naïve CD8+ T cells are dysregulated during cHCV infection.
source: In sum, we provide the first evidence that naïve CD8+ T cells are dysregulated during cHCV infection, and establish a new mechanism of immune perturbation secondary to chronic infection.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a key finding in the abstract.

claim: The study establishes a new mechanism of immune perturbation secondary to chronic infection.
source: In sum, we provide the first evidence that naïve CD8+ T cells are dysregulated during cHCV infection, and establish a new mechanism of immune perturbation secondary to chronic infection.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a key finding in the abstract.

claim: Functional impairments of CD8+ T cells have been characterized in several persistent viral infections.
source: Functional impairments of CD8+ T cells have been characterized in several persistent viral infections, including human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in humans, simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infection in macaques, and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection in mice (Ahmed and Rouse, 2006).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: Chronic infection skews memory/effector CD8+ T cell differentiation.
source: In particular, it has been shown that chronic infection skews memory/effector CD8+ T cell differentiation (Stelekati and Wherry, 2012), and drives virus-specific CD8+ T cells towards an « exhausted » phenotypic state, as marked by high expression of the programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) molecule (Kim and Ahmed, 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Chronic infection drives virus-specific CD8+ T cells towards an exhausted phenotypic state, as marked by high expression of PD-1.
source: In particular, it has been shown that chronic infection skews memory/effector CD8+ T cell differentiation (Stelekati and Wherry, 2012), and drives virus-specific CD8+ T cells towards an « exhausted » phenotypic state, as marked by high expression of the programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) molecule (Kim and Ahmed, 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Chronic infections have been reported to impair immune responses to unrelated infectious microbes in mouse models.
source: Chronic infections have also been reported to impair immune responses to unrelated infectious microbes in mouse models (Stelekati and Wherry, 2012; Richer et al., 2013), as well as in humans infected with HCV (Park and Rehermann, 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Chronic infections have been reported to impair immune responses to unrelated infectious microbes in humans infected with HCV.
source: Chronic infections have also been reported to impair immune responses to unrelated infectious microbes in mouse models (Stelekati and Wherry, 2012; Richer et al., 2013), as well as in humans infected with HCV (Park and Rehermann, 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: The phenomenon of impaired immune responses to unrelated infectious microbes correlates with an IFN stimulated gene (ISG) transcriptional signature.
source: This phenomenon correlates with a interferon (IFN) stimulated gene (ISG) transcriptional signature, suggesting an indirect effect of systemic type I IFN secondary to innate immune activation (Stelekati et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: The ISG transcriptional signature suggests an indirect effect of systemic type I IFN secondary to innate immune activation.
source: This phenomenon correlates with a interferon (IFN) stimulated gene (ISG) transcriptional signature, suggesting an indirect effect of systemic type I IFN secondary to innate immune activation (Stelekati et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: The T cell preimmune repertoire plays an important role in shaping the adaptive immune responses.
source: Following from these observations, we hypothesized that chronic infection may alter the T cell preimmune repertoire, which plays an important role in shaping the adaptive immune responses (Jenkins and Moon, 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: The α/β T cell preimmune repertoire is defined as the set of mature but antigen inexperienced lymphocytes that circulate in blood and secondary lymphoid organs.
source: The α/β T cell preimmune repertoire is defined as the set of mature but antigen inexperienced lymphocytes that circulate in blood and secondary lymphoid organs, ready to be activated by cognate high-affinity peptide-class I MHC (pMHC) complexes (Jenkins et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study providing this definition.

claim: Naïve T cells are maintained in the periphery by survival factors such as IL-7, as well as transient contacts with low affinity non-cognate pMHC complexes.
source: They are maintained in the periphery by survival factors such as IL-7, as well as transient contacts with low affinity non-cognate pMHC complexes (Sprent and Surh, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: The number of antigen-specific T cells (precursor frequency) is not equivalent across inexperienced populations.
source: First, the number of antigen-specific T cells (i.e. precursor frequency) is not equivalent across inexperienced populations, with the absolute number positively correlating with the magnitude of responses that are induced upon priming (Obar et al., 2008; Moon et al., 2007; Kwok et al., 2012; Schmidt et al., 2011; Kotturi et al., 2008; Tan et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: The absolute number of antigen-specific T cells positively correlates with the magnitude of responses that are induced upon priming.
source: First, the number of antigen-specific T cells (i.e. precursor frequency) is not equivalent across inexperienced populations, with the absolute number positively correlating with the magnitude of responses that are induced upon priming (Obar et al., 2008; Moon et al., 2007; Kwok et al., 2012; Schmidt et al., 2011; Kotturi et al., 2008; Tan et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Antigen-inexperienced CD4+ and CD8+ T cell populations contain variable proportions of memory-phenotype (MP) cells.
source: Second, antigen-inexperienced CD4+ and CD8+ T cell populations contain variable proportions of memory-phenotype (MP) cells (Legoux et al., 2010; Su et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Memory-phenotype cells in antigen-inexperienced populations have been explained in the literature as a result of cross-reactivity or homeostatic proliferation.
source: These cells have been explained in the literature as a result of cross-reactivity or homeostatic proliferation (Sprent and Surh, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this explanation.

claim: Cross-reactivity is now recognized as an essential feature of the T-cell receptor (TCR) / MHC interaction.
source: Cross-reactivity is now recognized as an essential feature of the T-cell receptor (TCR) / MHC interaction (Mason et al., 1998), and a major determinant of virus-specific MP cells in the CD4+ T cell repertoire of unexposed healthy donors (Su et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Cross-reactivity is a major determinant of virus-specific MP cells in the CD4+ T cell repertoire of unexposed healthy donors.
source: Cross-reactivity is now recognized as an essential feature of the T-cell receptor (TCR) / MHC interaction (Mason et al., 1998), and a major determinant of virus-specific MP cells in the CD4+ T cell repertoire of unexposed healthy donors (Su et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: Homeostatic proliferation may occur in settings of lymphopenia.
source: Alternatively, homeostatic proliferation may occur in settings of lymphopenia (Jones et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: Differential CD5 expression by antigen-specific T cell populations has been shown to dictate clonal recruitment and expansion.
source: Finally, differential CD5 expression by antigen-specific T cell populations has been shown to dictate clonal recruitment and expansion (Fulton et al., 2015; Tabbekh et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: The impact of non-heritable influences such as human chronic viral infection on the quantitative and qualitative aspects of the preimmune repertoire remains unknown.
source: To date, the impact of non-heritable influences such as human chronic viral infection on the quantitative and qualitative aspects of the preimmune repertoire remains unknown.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection show CD8+ T cell dysfunction.
source: In our study, we focused on patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection (cHCV), which show CD8+ T cell dysfunction (Park and Rehermann, 2014; Rehermann and Nascimbeni, 2005).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies reporting this finding.

claim: HCV-specific responses are typically weak in terms of numbers and function.
source: In particular, HCV-specific responses are typically (i) weak – both in term of numbers and function, (ii) of low avidity, and (iii) blocked in their differentiation into central memory cells, despite the availability of cognate pMHC complexes (Park and Rehermann, 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: HCV-specific responses are typically of low avidity.
source: In particular, HCV-specific responses are typically (i) weak – both in term of numbers and function, (ii) of low avidity, and (iii) blocked in their differentiation into central memory cells, despite the availability of cognate pMHC complexes (Park and Rehermann, 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: HCV-specific responses are typically blocked in their differentiation into central memory cells, despite the availability of cognate pMHC complexes.
source: In particular, HCV-specific responses are typically (i) weak – both in term of numbers and function, (ii) of low avidity, and (iii) blocked in their differentiation into central memory cells, despite the availability of cognate pMHC complexes (Park and Rehermann, 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study reporting this finding.

claim: cHCV is to date the only chronic viral infection that can be cured.
source: cHCV is to date the only chronic viral infection that can be cured, offering the unique possibility to interrogate the reversibility of immune perturbations post-viral clearance (Pol et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study and states this as established knowledge.

claim: The positive effect of chronic infection on naïve T cell recruitment into immune responses is transient.
source: Importantly, the positive effect of chronic infection on naïve T cell recruitment into immune responses is transient, as cHCV patients who clear their virus following successful therapy (referred to as Sustained Virologic Responders or SVR) can experience a reversion towards a healthy naïve T cell repertoire within 2 years.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: cHCV patients who clear their virus following successful therapy can experience a reversion towards a healthy naïve T cell repertoire within 2 years.
source: Importantly, the positive effect of chronic infection on naïve T cell recruitment into immune responses is transient, as cHCV patients who clear their virus following successful therapy (referred to as Sustained Virologic Responders or SVR) can experience a reversion towards a healthy naïve T cell repertoire within 2 years.

claim: The data highlight the added benefit of early viral clearance in patients with chronic HCV infection.
source: These data provide the first evidence for chronic infection resulting in the bystander dysregulation of the antigen-specific preimmune repertoire in humans, and highlight the added benefit of early viral clearance in patients with chronic HCV infection.
evidence: The manuscript provides an interpretation based on the data presented.
